decisions.reason: DDL/DML/DCL and access-control design do not require aggregation or GROUP BY. Given a table Member(id,name), creating it, inserting a row, and granting/revoking SELECT to a reader can be acquired without aggregation. The already required basic SQL goal remains; its full join/sort breadth and current Q1-exam predecessor are not newly certified as minimal by this bounded correction.

Time-ordered method calls between participating objects and services use the class/object/method concepts in cb2. Independent calls can be modelled in a parallel sequence fragment without a relational schema or normalization to 3NF. The exact description adds modelling concurrency/services as the new performance; requiring a POP/SMTP-specific goal would be unnecessary. The current cb2-to-E-exam path remains an open earlier prerequisite finding.

Classifying TLS, authentication/authorization and firewall protection needs client/server risks and identities, which the existing foundation provides. Distinguishing WLAN eavesdropping from missing role rights and an exposed database port does not require binary/hex arithmetic or two-complement calculations. The proposed Q4 C1 task provides this additional concrete context; this is no source, practice, or effectiveness approval.
